merger_name: Blackstone funds and Perpetual Trustees – HSBC loan portfolio

anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
Virgo BidCo Pty Ltd (**BidCo**), an affiliate of certain funds advised and/or managed by affiliates of Blackstone Inc. (**Blackstone**), proposes to acquire HSBC Bank Australia Limited’s (**HBAU**) portfolio of Australian home and personal loans (the **Acquisition**).

BidCo intends to direct that title in these loans be transferred at completion to Perpetual Corporate Trust Limited (**Perpetual**) in its capacity as trustee of three securitisation trusts. Perpetual will appoint Pepper Money Limited under contractual servicing arrangements to undertake the operational management and administration of the loans.

Certain home loans originated by HBAU are held within four existing securitisation trusts – the Lion Series 2020-1 Trust, Lion Series 2022 1 Trust, Lion Series 2023-1 Trust and Lion Series 2024-1 Trust (together, the **Lion Trusts**). As part of the Acquisition, BidCo will nominate ABF Whole Loan Pty Ltd (an affiliate of certain funds advised and/or managed by affiliates of Blackstone, and BidCo’s parent) to acquire the sole participation unit and 9 of the 10 residual units in each of the Lion Trusts. Perpetual CT Capital Pty Ltd (a Perpetual Group entity) will acquire 1 of the 10 residual units in each of these trusts.

Blackstone is a US-based investment management firm.

Perpetual is a Sydney-based trust company and a wholly-owned subsidiary within the Perpetual group of companies (**Perpetual Group**), of which Perpetual Limited is the ultimate parent company.

HBAU is the Australian-owned subsidiary of HSBC Holdings plc (including its affiliates, **HSBC**). HBAU currently offers a range of financial services in Australia, including retail banking, private banking, asset management and corporate and institutional banking. HSBC has announced it intends to exit its retail banking operations in Australia.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
finds that the Acquisition would have a limited effect on competition
in the supply home and personal loans in Australia, given:
• HSBC’s intention to exit its retail banking operations in
Australia
• the Acquisition is limited to the sale of a ‘back book’ of
loans to parties that are not active in the supply of home
and personal loans in Australia.
